text: Every episode of a show has an intro, and nothing tells you where it is.
I wanted a skip intro button anyway, so Watch listens for it.
It turns the audio into one channel at eight kilohertz.
Thirty-one times a second, it checks how the loudness shifts between neighbouring pitches.
Thirty-three bands, from the low end of a voice to the top of it.
Each moment becomes a thirty-two bit hash, a tiny barcode of the sound.
It's written in plain Node, because the ffmpeg build had no fingerprint library.

text: Now take two episodes from the same season.
Watch slides one barcode strip past the other.
Where the same theme song plays, the hashes line up and light up.
One match could be luck, so other episodes vote.
The stretch most of them share is the intro.
If only one episode agrees, it gets flagged instead of trusted.
Finally the edges snap to the nearest cut in the picture.
Skip intro lands right where the story starts, with nobody marking a thing.
